title: Database indexes
description: What an index buys, what it costs, and how to tell whether a query is using one.

questions.text: What does an index mainly speed up?

options.text: Reads that filter or sort on the indexed columns

questions.explanation: An index is an ordered structure the database can search instead of scanning the whole table.

questions.text: Every additional index makes writes to the table slower.
questions.explanation: Each insert, update or delete must also maintain every index on the table, and each index takes space.

questions.text: A composite index on (last_name, first_name) can efficiently serve which query?
questions.explanation: A composite index is ordered by its first column, then the second. A query must use a leftmost prefix of the columns to benefit.

questions.text: Which columns usually deserve an index? Select all that apply.

options.text: A foreign key used in frequent joins
A column in the WHERE clause of a hot query
A boolean column with a 50/50 split, filtered alone on a huge table

questions.explanation: Index what queries actually filter and join on. Low-selectivity columns rarely help on their own, and indexing everything slows writes.

questions.text: EXPLAIN shows a sequential scan on a large table even though an index exists. What is a likely cause?

options.text: The query wraps the indexed column in a function, so the index cannot be used

questions.explanation: WHERE lower(email) = ... cannot use a plain index on email. Rewrite the predicate or create an index on the expression. Stale statistics are the other usual suspect.
